correctness.rationale: The defining predicate is exactly the 171 nonempty hitting constraints (18 balls and 153 pairwise symmetric differences), equivalently distinct nonzero closed-neighborhood signatures. Both independent complete programs verified a minimum size of nine and the entire 1028-code state set in isomorphic LCF and affine-incidence models. All 9×9 possible replacements from each minimum code were tested; BFS from each vertex of every nontrivial component establishes exact radii, diameters, eccentricity distributions and component sizes. All declared numerical invariants agree and the graph isomorphism and side-swapping automorphism are directly checked. Finite exhaustive work proves only the stated finite theorem.

value.rationale: A complete optimum-code census and the exact mobility geometry on the 18-vertex symmetric Pappus incidence graph answer natural, self-contained combinatorial questions about efficient fault-location sensors. The theorem exhibits two distinct mobility barriers: the code bipartition majority cannot be crossed even by arbitrary replacements, and local moves freeze 108 configurations even though those configurations still have permitted jumps. The 1028-state balance distribution, 460/514 component sizes and exact radius/diameter provide meaningful reproducible invariants not implied by known graph symmetry or the minimum cardinality. It is not a routine renaming, arbitrary slice or merely a general bound.
